title: How subagents work in Claude Code

beats.label: Main agent
beats.title: The main agent and its context window
beats.text: Your Claude Code session is one agent with one context window. Everything it reads, runs and says piles up in that column, and the space is finite.
beats.narration: On the left is your main Claude Code session. The glass column is its context window. As you chat and it reads files and runs commands, everything piles up in there, and that space is limited.

beats.label: Spawn
beats.title: It hands a task to a subagent
beats.text: Calling the Agent tool starts a general-purpose subagent with a brand-new, empty context. The only thing it receives is the prompt the main agent writes for it.
beats.narration: When a task is big or noisy, the main agent calls the Agent tool. A new general-purpose subagent appears on the right with a completely empty context window. The gold packet is the only thing it gets: the prompt the main agent wrote. It can't see your conversation, so that prompt has to say everything.

beats.label: Work
beats.title: The subagent does the messy work
beats.text: It has the same tools: it searches, reads files and runs commands. All of that fills the subagent's context, not the main one.
beats.narration: Now the subagent goes to work on the codebase, searching, reading files, running commands. Watch its column fill up with all of that. Look at the main agent's column on the left: it hasn't moved.

beats.label: Parallel
beats.title: Several can run side by side
beats.text: Independent tasks can go to several subagents at once. Each gets its own fresh context and works in isolation from the others.
beats.narration: If there are independent pieces of work, the main agent can start several subagents at the same time. Each one gets its own prompt and its own fresh context, and they work in parallel without seeing each other.

beats.label: Report back
beats.title: Only a summary comes back
beats.text: When a subagent finishes, its final message returns to the main agent as the tool result. Its working context is thrown away.
beats.narration: When each subagent finishes, it sends back one final message, the green packets. That summary is all the main agent receives. Everything the subagent read along the way is discarded, and the subagents disappear.

beats.label: The payoff
beats.title: Big work, small footprint
beats.text: The main context grew by a thin green slice of conclusions instead of every file read. That's why subagents help long sessions stay focused.
beats.narration: Here's the payoff. The main agent's context grew by just that thin green slice of conclusions, rather than by every file the subagents read. That keeps long sessions focused, and the work could happen in parallel too.
